models.name: economic_board_citizens
models.description: Main actor table for standard users. Stores email, password_hash, display_name, bio, and account status. Email is unique and required. All citizens have is_admin=false and is_super_admin=false.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: User's email address for authentication. Must be unique across the system.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hash of the user's password. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public-facing name displayed on articles and comments. Can be changed by user.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional short biography or introduction about the user.

plainFields.name: is_banned
plainFields.description: Flag indicating if the account has been banned. When true, user cannot log in and all sessions are revoked.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by administrator for banning this user. Must be at least 10 characters when is_banned is true.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the user account was created. Set once and never changed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last modification to the user profile. Updated on display_name, bio, or password changes.

models.name: economic_board_administrators
models.description: Main actor table for standard administrators (not super administrators). Stores email, password hash, account status, and admin-specific fields. This table is exclusively for users promoted to administrator role but not super administrator. It has its own session, password reset, and audit trail records. All super administrators are stored in a separate table, economic_board_super_administrators, following the actor separation principle.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address for authentication. Must be verified before login.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt-hashed password. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown on articles and comments. Can be modified by user.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional self-description briefly explaining the user's expertise or interest.

plainFields.name: is_banned
plainFields.description: If true, user is banned and cannot authenticate. True by default when banned.

plainFields.name: ban_reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by the banning administrator. Required when is_banned is true.

plainFields.name: admin_request_status
plainFields.description: Status of the administrator promotion request from citizen: pending, approved, or rejected.

plainFields.name: admin_request_reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the citizen when requesting promotion to administrator.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator record was last updated.

models.name: economic_board_super_administrators
models.description: This table is marked for deletion. It is a redundant duplicate of economic_board_administrators and violates the single-actor-per-table principle. Do not create this table. The superAdministrator role is managed via is_super_admin flag in economic_board_administrators.

models.name: economic_board_citizen_sessions
models.description: Session table for citizen users. Stores JWT access token, refresh token, device fingerprint, and expiration times. Tied to citizen via user_id. Append-only audit trail of login events, managed through authentication flows, not direct user CRUD.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen user account. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token issued for this session.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token issued for this session, stored as hash for security.

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique identifier derived from browser/user agent properties to detect device changes.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Full URL of the page from which the login request originated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referer header value indicating previous website or page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Always required.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires. Default is 14 days from creation.

models.name: economic_board_administrator_sessions
models.description: Session table for administrator and super administrator users. Stores connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) and session expiration times. Append-only audit trail of login events. Linked to economic_board_administrators via foreign key.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator's {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address of login session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Current page URL when session was created.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led to login.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Default is 7 days from created_at.

models.name: economic_board_super_administrator_sessions
models.description: Session table for super administrator users. Stores JWT access token, refresh token, device fingerprint, and expiration times. Tied to super administrator via user_id. This table is redundant with economic_board_administrator_sessions and will be removed in next version.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator actor table. This is a technical placeholder; in reality, this table should not exist and super administrators share the same session table as administrators.

plainFields.name: access_token
plainFields.description: JWT access token for session authentication.

plainFields.name: refresh_token
plainFields.description: JWT refresh token stored in secure cookie.

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the device used in the session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Never null per security policy.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated.

models.name: economic_board_citizen_password_resets
models.description: Password reset tokens for citizen users. Contains a secure token, expiration timestamp, and user_id. Generated when a citizen requests a password reset. Token is single-use and becomes invalid after use or expiration. Tokens are purged after successful reset or expiration, not logically deleted.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: References the citizen user requesting the password reset. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Secure, randomly generated password reset token. Must be unguessable and unique per request.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the password reset token. Token becomes invalid after this time.

models.name: economic_board_citizen_email_verifications
models.description: Email verification tokens for citizens. Contains secure token, expiration timestamp, and user_id. Sent during registration and re-sent upon request. This is a transient verification table with one-time use tokens. Records are deleted after successful verification or expiration.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: References the citizen account that requested verification. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique, secure, random token for email verification. Must be cryptographically secure and URL-safe.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the verification token. After this time, the token is invalid and must be regenerated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token was generated.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was last updated (e.g., resent).

plainFields.name: is_used
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether the token has been successfully used to verify the email address.

models.name: economic_board_administrator_audit_logs
models.description: Audit trail for all administrative actions. Records actor_id, target_id, action_type (ban, promote, delete, etc.), reason, timestamp, and IP address. Captures all actions by administrators and super administrators. Each record is immutable and append-only. Used for forensic accountability, regulatory compliance, and privilege monitoring.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed the action. References economic_board_administrators.id.

foreignFields.name: target_id
foreignFields.description: The user (citizen or administrator) who was acted upon. References economic_board_citizens.id or economic_board_administrators.id. Nullable when action targets system resources, not users.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of administrative action performed. Values: 'ban', 'unban', 'promote', 'demote', 'delete_article', 'delete_comment', 'delete_section', 'approve_admin_request', 'reject_admin_request'.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The administrative reason for the action (e.g., policy violation, inappropriate content). Limited to 500 characters by application logic.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the action was performed. Used for geo-location and abuse detection.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was created. Always set by server.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the log entry. Always equal to created_at as entries are immutable.

models.name: economic_board_administrator_password_resets
models.description: Password reset tokens for administrator accounts. Stores secure reset tokens with expiration timestamps. Used during password recovery flow for administrator type users. Each token is single-use and tied to one administrator. Separate from citizen password reset table to enforce actor-specific security boundaries.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: References the administrator account requesting the password reset. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Secure, random, single-use token used to reset the password. Must be cryptographically random and URL-safe.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: DateTime when this reset token expires and becomes invalid. After this time, the token cannot be used for password reset.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: DateTime when the reset request was created and token was generated.

models.name: economic_board_super_administrator_password_resets

foreignFields.name: super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: References the superAdministrator actor account that requested the password reset. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Secure, randomly generated token used for password reset. Must be unique per reset request.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token expires. After this time, the token becomes invalid and cannot be used.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

models.name: economic_board_articles
models.description: Main article entries with title, content, author, and section reference. Articles represent user-submitted content within a section. Articles can be edited by the original author within the edit window (2 hours) and deleted by authors or administrators. Deleted articles retain their record with is_deleted=true for audit purposes. Comments and attachments are linked via foreign keys but stored separately to maintain normalization.

foreignFields.name: section_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the section this article belongs to. {@link economic_board_sections.id}

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen who created this article. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the article. Must be between 5 and 200 characters, trimmed of whitespace.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Full content of the article. Must be at least 10 characters, up to 50,000 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the article was created. Always set to server time (Asia/Seoul).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the article was last edited. Updated on every content modification.

plainFields.name: is_deleted
plainFields.description: Soft delete flag. If true, article is hidden from public views but preserved in database for audit purposes.

models.name: economic_board_sections
models.description: Content sections where articles are categorized and managed by administrators. Each section defines a top-level category for organizing articles (e.g., Politics, Economy). Administrators create, edit, and delete sections independently. Sections have unique names to prevent ambiguity. Soft deletion is implemented via deleted_at to preserve history for associated articles without cascading deletion.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique name of the section (e.g., 'Economy', 'Politics'). Must be unique across all active sections. Case-insensitive comparison enforced by unique index.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Brief description explaining the section's purpose and scope. Used in UI to guide users on content expectations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created. Immutable.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last updated. Updated automatically on any edit.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was logically deleted. NULL indicates active section. Non-NULL indicates deleted status. Used for soft deletion and audit.

models.name: economic_board_comments
models.description:
User comments attached to articles, linked by article_id and author_id. Each comment is an independent entity that can be searched, filtered, edited, and deleted by its author or moderated by administrators. Comments are not owned by articles but are associated with them via foreign key, enabling cross-article comment queries and moderation workflows. Always references citizen from Systematic component. Track creation and update times for audit. Allow soft deletion for compliance and moderation workflows. Support full-text search on content for user search functionality. Never store JSON, arrays, or derived values. Follow 3NF with no transitive dependencies.

For API operations:
- POST /comments creates a new comment
- GET /comments?article_id=...&limit=20&sort=newest lists comments by article
- PATCH /comments/{id} edits comment (within 60-minute window)
- DELETE /comments/{id} deletes comment (deleted_at timestamp)
- GET /search/comments?q=... searches comment content using GIN index

Relationships:
- Comment is owned by citizen only; administrators can delete but are not owners as per permission matrix.
- Comments do not form a hierarchy; replies are out of scope for this version.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: The article this comment is associated with. {@link economic_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who authored this comment. {@link economic_board_citizens.id}

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Plain text content of the comment, up to 1000 characters. Required and trimmed of whitespace.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when comment was created. Always recorded in Asia/Seoul timezone.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when comment was last edited. Updated on every edit. Used for edit window validation (1-hour).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when comment was soft-deleted. If null, comment is active. Used for moderation and audit purposes.

models.name: economic_board_article_tags
models.description: Junction table that associates articles with their tags in a many-to-many relationship. Each row represents one tag applied to one article, enabling efficient filtering and preventing tag duplication. Tag strings are stored as-is to support free-form user input while maintaining referential integrity through composite unique index. Used for search filtering and content categorization.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_article_id
foreignFields.description: References the article being tagged. {@link economic_board_articles.id}. Required for normalization.

plainFields.name: tag
plainFields.description: The actual tag string provided by the user. Free-form text, trimmed of whitespace on input. Maximum 50 characters as per requirements. Case-insensitive uniqueness enforced via unique index.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tag was first applied to the article.

models.name: economic_board_article_attachments
models.description:
Metadata for files and images attached to articles, including URL, type, and size. This is a subsidiary entity—managed exclusively through articles and not directly by users. Each file or image upload creates a separate record. Retained for audit purposes even after article deletion.

Business context: This table holds critical metadata for media attachments (files and images) uploaded by users. The system tracks: exact file URL (for CDN access), original filename, MIME type (e.g., image/jpeg), file size in bytes, and upload timestamp. Used by the frontend to display previews and enable downloads. Must be immutable after upload.

Relationships:
- Belongs to one article (one-to-many) via article_id
- Used in article views to render attachments
- Audited via economic_board_administrator_audit_logs when manually deleted

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent article this attachment belongs to. {@link economic_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: file_url
plainFields.description: CDN-accessible URL where the file or image is stored.

plainFields.name: file_name
plainFields.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user. Preserved exactly for download.

plainFields.name: file_type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., image/png, application/pdf). Determined by file headers, not extension.

plainFields.name: file_size
plainFields.description: Size of the file in bytes. Used for bandwidth estimation and quota tracking.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded. Set server-side on insert.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp last modified. Always equals created_at unless explicitly edited (rare). Set on insert and update.

models.name: economic_board_article_snapshots
models.description: Point-in-time snapshots of article state for audit and historical retrieval. Captures the exact state of an article at the moment it was saved, preserving changes for compliance and version tracking. The original economic_board_articles record may be edited or deleted, but snapshots remain immutable. Used to display historical versions of articles and audit editing activity. Reference original article via article_id. This table only tracks the snapshot creation context - tags and attachments are stored in separate subsidiary tables: economic_board_article_snapshot_tags and economic_board_article_snapshot_attachments.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original article being snapshotted. {@link economic_board_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created (not the original article creation time).

plainFields.name: snapshot_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for snapshot creation: "initial", "edit", "deletion", "admin_delete".

models.name: economic_board_section_snapshots
models.description: Point-in-time snapshots of section name and description to audit how sections evolved over time. Each snapshot records the exact state of a section at the moment it was modified. References the original section via section_id. Used to reconstruct historical versions of sections, track changes, and ensure accountability in administrative edits. Snapshots are append-only and never modified after creation.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_section_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original section record. {@link economic_board_sections.id}

foreignFields.name: economic_board_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who triggered this snapshot via edit. {@link economic_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: section_name
plainFields.description: The name of the section at the time of this snapshot.

plainFields.name: section_description
plainFields.description: The description of the section at the time of this snapshot.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Always matches the edit timestamp of the source section.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for consistency with other models. Always equals created_at since snapshots are immutable.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Always NULL; snapshots are never soft-deleted as they represent historical audit data.

plainFields.name: snapshot_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the snapshot creation (e.g. 'section edited', 'section deleted').

models.name: economic_board_article_views
models.description: Tracks views of articles by users for analytics and popularity ranking. Each record represents a unique view by a user during a session. Data is used to compute popular articles, trending content, and user engagement metrics. Note: user_id references either economic_board_citizens or economic_board_administrators via polymorphic relationship using user_type and user_id. Views are timestamped to enable time-series analysis and hourly/daily popularity tracking.

foreignFields.name: article_id
foreignFields.description: References the article being viewed. {@link economic_board_articles.id}

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: References the viewing user (either citizen or administrator). {@link economic_board_citizens.id} or {@link economic_board_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: user_type
plainFields.description: Type of user: 'citizen' or 'administrator'. Required to disambiguate polymorphic reference when user_id is used across multiple tables.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of when the view occurred. Used for time-series analytics, trend analysis, and calculating view counts over time periods.

models.name: economic_board_tags
models.description:
Master catalog of unique tags used across articles. Each tag is stored once, and article_tags table references this table via tag_id. This ensures 3NF compliance, avoids string duplication, and enables consistent tagging and filtering.

Tags are managed independently by the system: they are auto-created when first used, and preserved even if no article references them. Used in search, filtering, and analytics. Never deleted unless manually purged by admin.

plainFields.name: tag
plainFields.description: The normalized tag string, stored in lowercase. Must be unique across the system. Max 50 characters. Trims whitespace on insertion. Example: 'economics'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tag was first created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update. Updates when the tag string is edited (though edits are rare).

models.name: economic_board_attachment_types
models.description:
Master catalog of attachment MIME type categorizations (e.g., image/jpeg → image) for standardized handling across the system. This lookup table normalizes MIME types into categorical groups to avoid redundancy in article_attachments. When a file is uploaded, its MIME type is stored as a string here and referenced in article_attachments, ensuring consistent handling of file types (image, document, video, etc.) without duplicating full MIME type strings in every attachment record.

Used in article_attachments to categorize attachments for UI rendering and filtering. For example, when displaying 'image' category, the system queries this table for all mime_types mapped to 'image', then finds all article_attachments matching those mime_types.

Must be seeded with common MIME types from the file type allowlist: text/plain, application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, video/mp4, audio/mp3, application/zip, application/octet-stream, etc.

plainFields.name: mime_type
plainFields.description: The complete MIME type string (e.g., 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf'). Must be unique and match exactly the Content-Type header from upload. This is the primary key (not ID) to ensure referential integrity and avoid duplication.

plainFields.name: category
plainFields.description: The standardized category group for this MIME type. Values are: 'image', 'document', 'video', 'audio', 'archive', or 'other'. Maps broad categories for UI filtering and display logic.

models.name: economic_board_article_snapshot_tags
models.description:
Snapshot of tag associations for a specific article version. Stores which tags were applied to the article at the exact moment the article snapshot was created. Each record links a snapshot to one tag. This table is necessary for 1NF compliance as tags are a repeating group that cannot be stored as comma-separated strings.

This table is a subsidiary entity, only accessed via parent article snapshots. It is never created, updated, or deleted independently by users. It supports audit trails and historical tag analysis for article revisions.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_article_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article snapshot this tag association belongs to. {@link economic_board_article_snapshots.id}.

foreignFields.name: economic_board_tag_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the tag being applied. {@link economic_board_tags.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this tag association was recorded in the snapshot.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When this tag association was last updated (typically same as created_at, for consistency).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if not deleted.

models.name: economic_board_article_snapshot_attachments
models.description: Junction table for attaching files and images to article snapshots. Each record links one article snapshot (economic_board_article_snapshots.id) to one attachment (economic_board_article_attachments.id). This table is required for 1NF compliance as attachments are a repeating group that cannot be stored as arrays or JSON. Preserves the exact state of attachments at the time the article snapshot was created. This table is not accessed directly by users but is used internally for historical versioning and audit purposes. Linked to @\link economic_board_article_snapshots and @\link economic_board_article_attachments.

foreignFields.name: article_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article snapshot this attachment belongs to. A snapshot may have multiple attachments. @\link economic_board_article_snapshots.id.

foreignFields.name: article_attachment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the actual file attachment. This links to a single attachment record in economic_board_article_attachments. @\link economic_board_article_attachments.id.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot-attachment link was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot-attachment link was last updated. Always equal to created_at since this table is append-only.
